# Affine — MATH mining, verification and training

Dashboard: https://affine.io/
Live mining discovery: https://affine.io/mining.json
Measurements: https://affine.io/network-data.json
Code: https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine (main)
Signed payout eligibility policy: https://affine.io/reward-policy.json

## Sampling cutover

Cutover state: active from epoch nonpayable-live-reward-math-v1--1791128338-9. This epoch requires exact forced-sampler replay. Check mining.json and the signed manifest for current upload availability.

The replacement source is 310492f6a87721760630b196e375bd2ba43cbe05, with immutable bundle SHA256 e415623e5a8017133ff7bef3925b724441862f34b6d034ed0deb6b731a26e657. Later operator housekeeping commits do not change that bundle. Every epoch's signed manifest is authoritative; mining.json closes uploads during audits, training, evaluation or controller absence.

The new forced-inverse-cdf-replay-v1 contract binds epoch randomness, checkpoint, environment/task, bounded attempt number, turn and token position. Miner identity does not change the draws. The signed attempt budget is 128: attempt numbers 0 through 127. Miners can search these attempts for one success and one failure, but cannot select an arbitrary seed, substitute answers, change temperature/top-p or change the sampler. The approved v1 harness is text-tools-long-v2: uncached eager autoregressive computation, at most 1,024 output tokens per turn, temperature 0.8 and top-p 1. The signed manifest and source take precedence over this guide.

An expensive audit regenerates the complete audited output and requires exact token and stopping agreement, then independently checks full conditional probabilities, TOPLOC fingerprints and native grading. Wrong sampler picks have no match-rate or numerical-tolerance exemption. This establishes consistency with the prescribed computation and sampler; it does not prove historical execution or unbiased selection of successes and failures. TOPLOC without this replay cannot distinguish sampled outputs from copied answers passed through the model afterward.

Qualification used real H200 generation: one successful 746-token output and one failed 1,024-token output, independent replay with zero honest false rejections, and three rejected attacks. A copied correct answer with newly computed genuine probabilities and TOPLOC proofs passed the old verification but failed the new sampler check. A separate H200 verified the genuine pair through the production signed-job path, and the trainer independently re-audited it and performed a full-model covered update. These are qualification controls, not a completed new public epoch or a learning-gain claim. Details: https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/FORCED_SAMPLING_QUALIFICATION.md

Epoch eight completed its audits and scoring under its original signed rules. Its final three training updates were explicitly skipped after the original trainer rejected the disk reserve before issuing a job. The signed retirement is in R2 history. The new epoch inherits checkpoint 093 and fifteen cumulative updates; no legacy training success is claimed. They retain their scores, original evidence and writer cursor. The cutover is prospective; old-contract data cannot become new-contract reward or training evidence. The old burn and equal-registration writers remain disabled, and historical nonpayable experiments are not paid retroactively. The single reward writer preserves the signed policy for currently owned, eligible registered UIDs.

## Model and taskset

Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct has 7,615,616,512 parameters. Training updates all parameters in BF16. The active original MATH taskset contains 7,496 distinct usable problems: 6,746 mining tasks and 750 reserved held-out tasks. DeepMath and NuminaMath are not yet part of this contract. K=1 and L=1: one genuinely graded success and one genuinely graded failure for the same task on the approved checkpoint.

Held-out evaluation retains the previous precommitted sampler and fixed task/seed identities, so the sampling cutover does not redefine the measurement. Its outputs are diagnostic and cannot supply mining evidence. The latest completed fixed 32-task diagnostic was 20/32, after fifteen cumulative optimizer updates; this is below an earlier 22/32 and does not demonstrate sustained improvement or a larger benchmark result.

## How to start mining

Use a coding agent to read this guide and the repository guides, set up your
miner, watch discovery and diagnose failures. Keep watching this document and
GitHub main: fixes and upgrades will continue. Each epoch's signed source and
checkpoint take precedence over an older checkout. Never silently reuse an old
source, upload grant, deadline or model checkpoint.

Admission is open to every current subnet-120 identity with valid signed Affine
Ed25519 activation. There is no operator whitelist. Each epoch snapshots the
eligible identities; later activations enter a subsequent epoch. The signed
current manifest contains the actual eligible identity snapshot. Registration/activation is
separate from public dashboard access. Keep signing keys private.

Start with these concrete guides:
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/MINER_QUICKSTART.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/MATH_MINER_BOOTSTRAP.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/DISTRIBUTED_GPU_ROLES.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/FORCED_SAMPLING_CUTOVER.md

Use the exact runtime and hardware profile pinned in the signed manifest.
H200/SM90, CUDA BF16 eager, disabled TF32 and CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8
are the qualified profile. Core version pins are torch 2.14.0, transformers
5.14.1 and toploc 0.1.6. A package version alone does not qualify a different
GPU/runtime; follow the full setup/profile instructions. The manifest's numerical
policy is authoritative. Full output probability width is 152,064, distinct from
the tokenizer's 151,665 entries.

Read authority and current_url from https://affine.io/mining.json. Run the signed
source bootstrap using your private activated Ed25519 seed file:

CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 python -B -m subnet.source_bootstrap \
  --authority "$AFFINE_OPERATOR_AUTHORITY" \
  --current-url "$AFFINE_SIGNED_CURRENT_URL" \
  --source-cache /absolute/private/source-cache \
  --key /absolute/private/miner.key \
  --state /absolute/private/miner-state \
  --env-id affine_math --max-batches 3 --search-budget 24 --once

The authority public key is
3301134b38401196d006a621ac4a772bb4b0e6afa15a7d34a0d1ae5f2c630bcd.
The bootstrap authenticates the signed pointer/manifest, approved source archive
and checkpoint file hashes. It admits the original task snapshot and executes
that signed code. Source approval authorizes execution; it is not a sandbox.
Your agent should monitor new epochs and launch each only once, inspect original
process handles after faults and never restart solely because observation timed
out. Do not share your wallet key, decrypted private upload capability or R2
credentials. Miners need no permanent bucket credentials.

## Batch and reward rules

The current signed quota is three batches per UID per epoch, with artifact-size and rollout limits enforced independently. This is a conservative configurable pilot cap, not a protocol maximum. A batch covers one authorized mining task index on one epoch/checkpoint and includes complete input/output token contexts, full conditional log probabilities, TOPLOC fingerprints, native observations/outcomes, immutable task/model/source identities, and, for new-contract rollouts, the sampler receipt. Extra rollouts on the same task add no points. Grader errors and unsuccessful searches are not valid negative samples.

Uploads are cumulative replacements of one private epoch object, using an encrypted per-identity presigned capability. Replacements reuse the same three slots. Only the final completed in-window upload is frozen. Upload deadlines are not extended to rescue a worker. Frozen artifacts and authenticated audit history are published for inspection; miners do not need permanent R2 credentials.

Cheap bounded structure and quota checks apply to every submission. Expensive audits use the signed random allocation, minimum/maximum per identity, total budget and escalation rules. Reports bind the frozen batch hash, signed original request, approved source, exact checkpoint and winning job lease. Infrastructure faults trigger retries rather than fraud penalties. Only fully audited valid pairs earn points or enter training; observed cross-miner duplicate task keys receive zero for all competing miners. Unchecked duplicate claims remain unresolved and that limitation is recorded.

Adjusted points = unique fully verified task points * 0.5 ** invalid_batches.
Structural failures earn no batch points but do not multiply the remaining points. Epoch-zero thresholds are disabled in the current policy. Penalties reduce rewards; they do not take wallet funds. Exact adjusted points are summed over finalized epochs in the completed UTC hour and normalized across currently eligible owners. The writer waits for pending audits/final scores before closing their hour and does not treat unresolved work as zero. Every policy change applies prospectively through a signed manifest.

## Independent roles and durable history

Arbos.life is the operator host running the validator/controller, authenticated audit queue, single chain writer, discovery monitor and dashboard. The five original Lium H200 role machines provide one test miner, two independent verifiers, one trainer and one evaluator. Four additional verifier machines have been rented: one H200 and three H100s, adding $10.10/hour. The additional H200 passed three known-good original-input controls and is enrolled as the third verifier through a signed epoch-scoped workforce supplement. H100 and legacy GPU qualification remains pending; six active audit workers are not claimed. Original scientific contracts and numerical tolerances remain unchanged. Shared R2 stores signed manifests, frozen submissions, reports, scores, checkpoints and history. This dashboard is at affine.io; the Arbos website and DNS are unchanged.

Verifier nodes lease jobs and publish authenticated results. The current E9 controller runs sealed receipt-admission source 94ff74eb335e24d4702da2ec10cc0aee068076b003e6c0b13b0e81f5090bc79c and is held before training pending its final accepted receipt inventory. The admitted large H200 trainer has approximately 1.25 TB free. Receipt admission removes duplicate trainer inference, TOPLOC, sampling replay and environment audits: independent verifiers perform those checks once, and the operator issues a compact signed receipt from the original completed queue job and registered worker's signed report request. The trainer authenticates that receipt, checks the exact frozen ZIP hash/length and bounded structure, and trains only the committed fully audited success/failure pairs. It reports training_admissions, trainer_verification_performed=false and all_pairs_authenticated_verifier_receipts=true; it must not claim all_pairs_independently_reaudited. Training forward/backward and fixed-reference calculations remain training computations.

For current E9, a separate private authority-signed training-execution amendment must bind the original public challenge, exact accepted verifier receipt inventory, new training source and original three-update covered-v3 objective before the first train request. The original e415 miner/verifier/evaluator contract, checkpoint, sampler, task indices, harness and scoring remain unchanged. CP093's fifteen cumulative prior updates are not E9's requested step count. The new controller and training source have been admitted; no successful receipt-admitted GPU training is claimed yet. The controller is restricted to completing E9 and cannot automatically open the next epoch until all role sources are aligned. The historical qualification above used the original re-auditing trainer and remains historical evidence. Candidate details: https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/VERIFIER_RECEIPT_TRAINING.md

After admission, the trainer accumulates all accepted pairs across three configured full-model optimizer updates against the fixed input-checkpoint reference and publishes one immutable successor checkpoint. The synchronous next epoch waits for completed verification, training, held-out evaluation and publication. A configured step count is not evidence of completed training. Original completed training recovery must preserve the exact signed job, receipt inventory, amendment and report instead of issuing duplicate optimizer updates. Persistent-v4 additionally preserves the authority-committed latest parent state and optimizer counters even when the BF16 inference hash is unchanged; its new GPU qualification remains separate from current covered-v3 operation.

Automatic completed-download retention keeps R2 and original reports intact and removes only authenticated, completed local submission replicas after complete archive hash/size readback. It does not claim automatic retirement of every old model cache. Extra machines retained for independent qualification are outside the five live role nodes; this guide does not expand hardware approval to them.

The dashboard has two charts: matched held-out math performance over time and frozen submitted batches per finalized epoch. Submitted counts include rejected and unchecked batches; tooltips distinguish accepted totals. It displays observed results, not promised improvements.
